clue.text: Enlarge cover to support crest

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a comb is the fleshy crest on a cockerel's head

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a covering bigger so it can hold up a crest or plume.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cover' is a head of hair: backcombing teases it up to make it look fuller.
explanation.definitionFit: Backcombing means combing hair towards the scalp so that the hairstyle looks bigger and fuller.

clue.text: Walk in town to bone up on direct current period

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Walk in town to bone up on direct current period' builds BIRDCAGE (RIB reversed + DC + AGE, Birdcage Walk), but the file holds BIRD alone with no group linking 2-down CAGE
annotationWithheld.clue: Walk in town to bone up on direct current period

clue.text: see 1

annotationWithheld.why: 'see 1': second half of BIRDCAGE, but the file gives 1-down no group, so the linked answer cannot be annotated on its leader

clue.text: 1 down raised opposition to 18 26 by those who …

parts.note: 1 down in the printed grid is a bird, and a cock is one
something raised is up

explanation.surface: A bird holds up its objection to a famous kind of theory, on behalf of people who carry on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into the next one, whose answer names those who muddle through; their account of events is the cock-up theory, set against conspiracy theory (18 26).
explanation.definitionFit: The cock-up theory says disasters come from blunders rather than plots, the rival view to belief in secret schemes.

clue.text: … get there somehow — allow time to divide earth and flour with water

parts.note: mud is wet earth

indicators.note: the allowing and the time split the flour mixture by going into it

parts.note: dough is flour mixed with water
to let is to allow
hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: Recipe-like instructions to pause between mixing soil and making dough.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues from the previous clue's ellipsis. 'to divide' sends the allowing and the hour into the dough rather than between earth and dough.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle through is an idiom for reaching a goal somehow without proper planning or skill.

clue.text: Shakespearean bastard's name could be mud ultimately

indicators.note: says the letters could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: ultimately means in the end, giving end

explanation.surface: A remark that a villain's name will end up dragged through the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges MUD with END.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund is the illegitimate son of Gloucester in King Lear, famous for the speech defending bastards.

clue.text: Proclamation short of time is in time to make commitment

indicators.note: the shortened proclamation sits inside the second time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: a proclamation lacking the letter for time

parts.note: an edict is an official proclamation

explanation.surface: An announcement made with no time to spare arrives just in time to secure a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' drops T from EDICT, leaving EDIC, which 'is in' DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dedicate yourself to something is to commit to it wholeheartedly.

clue.text: In upper-class English rendering now blank and sure to remain so

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put inside the class marker and the nationality letter

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class speech and manners

indicators.note: a rendering is a version, so the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Translating a blank page into posh English is sure to leave it empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering' rearranges NOW BLANK into NKNOWABL, which goes 'In' U and E. The definition leans on the clue: what is blank and will stay so cannot ever be known.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unknowable can never be found out, so its blankness is certain to remain for good.

clue.text: Sweeten recalcitrant ladies with neat scotch?

indicators.note: unruly, refusing to stay in their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Uncooperative women take their whisky undiluted and need softening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalcitrant' rearranges LADIES and NEAT. 'Sweeten' is meant in the sense of making salt water fresh; 'scotch?' finishes the picture, as neat scotch is whisky without water.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten water in the old sense is to make it fresh, which is exactly removing its salt.

clue.text: Cromwell and co., say, in charge during journeys

indicators.note: the pieces come in the middle of the journeys

parts.note: rides are journeys
eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: Oliver Cromwell and his associates take charge while on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell was among those who signed the death warrant of Charles I in 1649.
explanation.definitionFit: Those responsible for executing Charles I are known as the regicides, killers of a king.

clue.text: Upwardly mobile person gets Arsenal player initially supple infiltrated by intelligence agency

indicators.note: the agency's letters get inside the footballer's name

parts.note: Sol Campbell, the Arsenal defender, with only the initial of his surname: Sol C
the CIA is the US intelligence agency
limber means supple

explanation.surface: A footballer, flexible and spied on by American agents, rises in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' shortens only the surname of Sol Campbell, Arsenal's centre back when this was set; the agency then works its way inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A social climber is someone eager to rise into a higher class, upwardly mobile in a pushy way.

clue.text: Pathetic turn about country composer

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the country
the word for pathetic is turned to read the other way

parts.note: sad means pathetic
UK is the United Kingdom, a country

explanation.surface: A sorry performance from a musician around the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes DAS from SAD, and that goes 'about' UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dukas was a French composer, best known for The Sorcerer's Apprentice.

clue.text: Rugby, say, makes player of piccolo blush

indicators.note: the letters are played with and turned into something else

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed into playing the piccolo in a school band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes player of' rearranges PICCOLO BLUSH. 'Rugby' is not the sport but the school where it began.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby School is a famous English fee-paying boarding school, the kind called a public school in Britain.

clue.text: Bit of by-play, perhaps, in which sleuths get points unintentionally

indicators.note: the detectives and points are put inside the stage phrase

parts.note: by-play read as by plus a bit of a play, which is an act
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives
E and N are compass points

explanation.surface: Detectives score points in a piece of stage business without meaning to.
explanation.walkthrough: By-play is stage business; splitting the hyphen gives 'by' plus a bit of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by accident means doing it without intending to.

clue.text: Spoiled new rattle — round the bend — products will be cracked

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the bend's letter
the rattle is spoiled, so its letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend in a pipe shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A baby's new rattle is broken and its owner is driven mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled' rearranges NEW RATTLE, and those letters go 'round' U. 'round the bend' looks like the idiom for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Walnuts grow on this tree, and the nuts must be cracked open before they are eaten.

clue.text: OK, OK, there's time

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, so OK
R stands for roger, said on the radio for OK

explanation.surface: Someone impatiently conceding that there is enough time.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time of twelve months.

clue.text: Players in tension with nostalgic conveyance

indicators.note: the players are placed inside the tension

parts.note: strain means tension
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Sportsmen under pressure travel on a heritage railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam train is the old form of rail transport that enthusiasts now ride for nostalgia.

clue.text: I provide maintenance for previous winner that doesn't start

indicators.note: the winner's title loses its first letter

parts.note: a cup-holder is last time's winner, still holding the trophy

explanation.surface: Last year's champion, who cannot even get going, claims to support the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that doesn't start' takes the C off CUPHOLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholder is one who supports or maintains something, such as a law or tradition.

clue.text: Studies theft as 23 to account for misfortune or …

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
piracy is theft, of ships or copyright

explanation.surface: Learning that robbery is the explanation for bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to THEORY in the printed numbering: a conspiracy theory blames misfortune on a plot. The clue runs on into the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy theory explains bad events as the work of secret plotters.

clue.text: … page number for land

parts.note: a lot is a number of things

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a page number gives a piece of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot also means conspiracy, tying it to the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a small piece of land, such as a building plot.

clue.text: Piece of cake including turn into drain

indicators.note: the cake portion holds the turn inside it

parts.note: a slice is a piece of cake
a U-turn is a turn, giving U

explanation.surface: A slice of cake gets turned and ends up down the drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' tempts as the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice is a channel with a gate for draining or controlling water.

clue.text: There entered on foot posh prophetess said to be up for presentation

parts.note: someone who walked in there trod in, giving in plus trod
U is the label for upper-class, posh

indicators.note: the word for a prophetess is spoken and gives a sound

parts.note: a sibyl is a prophetess of ancient times

explanation.surface: A grand seeress walks in, ready to be presented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns SIBYL into the sound of the ending -CIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something introducible can be introduced or presented, so it is fit to be put forward.

clue.text: Transmitter between 51 and 500 able to receive extended signals?

indicators.note: the transmitter splits the number letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral 50, followed by one
gear transmits power from engine to wheels
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A radio transmitter sits between two numbers, able to pick up distant broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 51 is read as L plus ONE, and GEAR goes in ONE before E. 'Transmitter' suggests radio but is mechanical gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ears would catch sounds from a distance, a joking picture of having long ears.

clue.text: A lot of capital musicians in addition

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, a band of musicians from the capital

explanation.surface: Plenty of London players are included as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means as well, in addition to what has been said.

clue.text: See 22
Spenserian rustic, fantastic creature without tail and head

indicators.note: the creature loses its last letter

parts.note: a hobbit is a creature of fantasy from Tolkien
noll is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A country character from Spenser is a fairy-tale beast lacking both tail and head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without tail' drops the T of HOBBIT. 'head' sounds like a deletion but supplies NOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbinoll is a shepherd in Spenser's The Shepheardes Calender, a country rustic.

clue.text: Idea of man in blue

indicators.note: the man is placed within the blue

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A notion belonging to a man dressed in blue, perhaps a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea put forward to explain something.

clue.text: Spread of notes on instrument topped by food at 10

indicators.note: the instrument has its top letter removed

parts.note: a harp is a musical instrument
an egg is food
10 written as I and O, the letter shapes of the digits

explanation.surface: Playing notes on an instrument with food delivered at ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the H from HARP to give ARP.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio plays the notes of a chord one after another, spread out rather than together.
